votes.reason: JPM is one of the money-center banks leading my Financials call (+1.72% into Warsh's hawkish close, +15% over 12 weeks), so it is the most direct way to own the one sector whose earnings improve if he means it.

PM is one of the two tobacco names my Staples call cites as leading (+1.94% in the week that ended with Warsh's hawkish Friday), so it is the defensive I want whichever way the jobs report breaks, though as one of the most dollar-exposed staples it would be hit first by my DXY-above-100 failure case.

Visa is one of the largest XLF holdings and sits at a record close (+2.85% on the week, +18% over 12 weeks), so it rides my Financials leadership call, though as a consumer-spending name it shares the soft-jobs risk I named rather than hedging it as the draft claims.

UNH gives my Healthcare call the low-volatility exposure I want for a data-heavy week (+0.73% in the week XLV lagged SPY by 2.45%) and has no stake in the biotech or GLP-1 risks of Monday's MFN round, even though it is a laggard (-5.18% over four weeks) rather than one of the breakout leaders.

REGN led the Healthcare advance (+25% over 12 weeks), so its 4.78% pullback should recover if Monday's MFN round clears the overhang as I expect, and as a large-cap biotech with no GLP-1 franchise it is neither one of the midsize names that round targets nor tied to the LLY risk I named.
